record.name: Notion
record.one_liner: Notion provides a REST API and SDKs allowing developers to automate workflows, read and write workspace pages, databases, and users through internal connections, personal access tokens, or OAuth 2.0 public connections.

auth.notes: Notion supports multiple authentication methods including static API tokens for internal connections, personal access tokens (PATs), and OAuth 2.0 for public connections.

access.notes: Developers can create personal access tokens or internal connections directly in the Developer portal.

api_surface.notes: The API supports RESTful conventions, webhooks for real-time events, and a JavaScript SDK.

buildability.reasoning: Credentials are self-serve (api_key) and the pages document a usable API surface. (Derived from access, auth and api_surface.)

evidence.claim: Notion supports internal connections, public connections, and personal access tokens powered by the REST API.
evidence.quote: For developers who want to build their own, Notion supports internal connections, public connections, and personal access tokens — all powered by the same REST API.

evidence.claim: The Notion API follows RESTful conventions and uses a bearer token.
evidence.quote: A bearer token is required to interact with the Notion API.

evidence.claim: Personal access tokens let users authenticate API requests.
evidence.quote: A personal access token (PAT) lets you authenticate API requests as yourself without setting up a connection or completing an OAuth flow.

evidence.claim: Connections can subscribe to real-time events via webhooks.
evidence.quote: Connections can subscribe to real-time events — like page updates, property changes, and new comments — via webhooks.

auth.quote: Notion supports three authentication models: Internal connections are scoped to a single workspace and use a static API token.

access.quote: Open Personal access tokens in the Developer portal.

api_surface.quote: With the REST API, you can read, create, and update nearly everything in a workspace — pages, databases, users, comments, and more.
